episodes.181906: A complex of thunderstorms dropped southeast into north central Alabama during the midday through mid afternoon hours. A few trees were knocked down as a result of the storms in Cullman County.
episodes.181908: Scattered thunderstorms developed ahead of an approaching cold front over Ohio and northwestern Pennsylvania during the early afternoon of August 12, 2023, and progressed eastward across central Pennsylvania through the late afternoon and evening hours. Sporadic wind damage (and one hail report) was observed with some of these storms, and there were two brief tornadoes in Cambria County.
episodes.181910: Numerous pulse thunderstorms crossed central Indiana from west to east from pre-dawn to mid-morning hours.  Despite several strong storms, a stable boundary layer prevented higher wind gusts from mixing down to the surface while a high freezing level melted larger hail aloft before it could reach the ground.  One marginally severe cell did, however, track southeastward across Johnson and Bartholomew Counties around 900 AM EDT.
episodes.181934: Abundant monsoon moisture surged into NM allowing for storms producing heavy rainfall and severe winds over portions of northeastern NM. Severe winds near Clayton, NM caused some damage on August 12th. Two more storms produced severe winds that were observed by automated weather stations at Santa Rosa and Tucumcari on August 13th. Heavy rainfall also produced flash flooding within the Hermit's Peak Calf Canyon burn scar during the afternoon. There were reports of debris and rocks washed across two state highways near Holman and Mora, and sandbags were deployed to protect homes in and around Rociada.
episodes.181998: A line of thunderstorms moved through Middle Tennessee during the early afternoon hours of August 12, 2023. Damaging straight-line winds were the main hazard with this line with numerous reports received of downed trees and powerlines. One weak tornado also occurred in Franklin, causing minor tree damage. This activity was produced a lot of lightning with notably caused a large apartment fire in Mount Juliet.
episodes.182083: Scattered showers and thunderstorms developed as a cold front moved through the Ohio Valley.
episodes.182104: Monsoon moisture moved into far northern Arizona and triggered a strong thunderstorm over the Arizona portion of Lake Powell.
episodes.182442: Isolated thunderstorms that formed late in the afternoon and evening of the 11th persisted into the early morning hours of the 12th as they moved across the Rolling Plains. One of these storms produced wind damage in far northeastern Childress County underneath a very dry sub-cloud layer. Several power poles were snapped as well as a tipped over center pivot irrigation system.
episodes.182497: An area of thunderstorms moved across far northern Illinois during the late evening of August 11th into the early morning of August 12th producing scattered wind damage.
episodes.182555: Scattered thunderstorms moved across portions of southern Lake Michigan during the late evening of August 11th and the early morning of August 12th.
episodes.182939: Scattered diurnal thunderstorms across southeast New Mexico resulted in localized strong winds.
episodes.183014: A broken line of strong thunderstorms became weaker and more disorganized as it moved south across southeast Missouri. However, outflow winds from these weakening storms were locally damaging shortly before they crossed into western Kentucky. The storms fed on a southwest wind flow of unstable air. The most unstable air was elevated, characterized by most-unstable layer capes around 2500 j/kg. The storms occurred ahead of a cold front that trailed southwest across the Ozarks from a low pressure center over the Great Lakes region.
episodes.183015: Clusters of strong thunderstorms over southeast Missouri and northwest Tennessee merged into a complex of severe thunderstorms over southwest Kentucky. Widespread damaging winds and a couple of isolated tornadoes accompanied the storms along the Tennessee border from Fulton and Hickman Counties eastward into south Graves County. Rainfall amounts ranging from 1 to 3 inches occurred across portions of western Kentucky. This included Fulton, Hickman, Graves, and Calloway counties. Much of this rain fell within 30 minutes to 1 hour. The storms weakened as they moved east across the Murray area, where heavy rain and street flooding was the main impact. The storms fed on a southwest wind flow of strongly unstable air. The most unstable air was slightly elevated, characterized by most-unstable layer capes around 2500 j/kg. Rather strong westerly mid-level winds around 40 knots provided sufficient vertical shear for this organized severe weather episode. The storms occurred ahead of a cold front that trailed southwest across the Ozarks from a low pressure center over the Great Lakes region. A subtle 500 mb shortwave in the west-northwest flow aloft aided the storms.
episodes.183218: A severe thunderstorm developed in the Sundance area and tracked southeastward before weakening as it moved into South Dakota. The storm produced hail to golf ball size.
episodes.183221: A supercell thunderstorm developed over the northern Black Hills and tracked southeast into the eastern Foothills and then onto the adjacent plains before weakening as it moved across the west central South Dakota plains. The storm produced hail larger than golf ball size and eventually strong wind gusts on the plains.
episodes.183222: A thunderstorm briefly became severe over the central Black Hills, producing quarter size hail near Sheridan Lake.
episodes.183223: A severe thunderstorm developed over the Custer area, with numerous reports of hail near ping pong ball size.
episodes.183370: Thunderstorms developed ahead of an approaching cold front and shortwave across Minnesota during the afternoon hours on Friday (8/11).  These storms tracked east through Wisconsin during the evening hours.  The strongest storms produced damaging winds and hail up to tennis ball size.
episodes.183373: Scattered thunderstorms produced strong winds over the bay of Green Bay during the evening hours on Friday (8/11).
episodes.183501: A frontal boundary moved through Central New York and supported multiple thunderstorms. High instability and shear supported scattered severe thunderstorms containing damaging wind gusts, large hail, and a NWS survey also confirmed a tornado in Delaware County. There were dozens of reports of trees down from other storms, with some trees falling onto occupied vehicles. Fortunately there were no injuries. There were also many reports of large hail with the largest size reported was 1.5 inches, which is about the size of a ping pong ball.
episodes.183502: A frontal boundary moved through Northeastern Pennsylvania, supporting multiple thunderstorms. High instability and shear supported isolated severe thunderstorms containing damaging wind gusts, small hail, and a tornado. NWS surveys confirmed a tornado in Luzerne County and a microburst in Bradford County. While most of the damage was downed trees from these events, there was some property damage as well.
episodes.183518: Marginally supportive shear and plenty of CAPE combine to produce numerous severe thunderstorms that grew upscale into a mesoscale convective system. This MCS progressed from west to east across eastern Tennessee, bringing numerous reports of damaging winds and isolated flash flooding.
episodes.183521: A mesoscale convective system that brought severe winds to east Tennessee continued to produce severe winds in North Carolina.
episodes.183638: Heavy rains from thunderstorms developed over much of the interior and southern portions of Puerto Rico on the 12th of August. This activity was associated with a surface trough and TUTT low.
episodes.183655: Thunderstorms developed across Wisconsin and moved out over Lake Michigan during the late evening and overnight hours. Thunderstorms produced strong winds in excess of 34 knots.
episodes.183700: Dangerously high heat index values combined with forcing from a passing mid-level short wave trough and approaching surface front triggered late day severe storms across SE GA.
episodes.183941: Strong thunderstorms along a cold front produced gusty winds across southern WI and one report of large hail.
episodes.184045: A shortwave disturbance moved out of Alabama and into North and Central Georgia along a nearly stationary frontal boundary. Overperforming instability and minor shear allowed thunderstorms to become strong to severe, particularly in the Atlanta Metro.
episodes.184077: After a warm front lifted across the region in the morning, the arrival of a strong upper level disturbance and surface cold front late in the day combined with ample instability and wind shear to produce severe thunderstorms to the southeast of Lake Ontario during the evening hours. Several reports of wind damage occurred. One storm that exhibited low-level rotation as it moved in off Lake Ontario to the southwest of Oswego produced wind damage with multiple reports of a rotating wall cloud and even a funnel cloud. However, a later survey of the area by county Emergency Management officials did not reveal any signs of tornadic storm damage.
episodes.184079: After a warm front lifted across the region in the morning, the arrival of a strong upper level disturbance and surface cold front late in the day combined with ample instability and wind shear to produce severe thunderstorms to the southeast of Lake Ontario during the evening hours. Several reports of wind damage occurred. One storm that exhibited low-level rotation as it moved in off Lake Ontario to the southwest of Oswego produced wind damage with multiple reports of a rotating wall cloud and even a funnel cloud. However, a later survey of the area by county Emergency Management officials did not reveal any signs of tornadic storm damage.
episodes.184338: On the afternoon of August 12th, strong to severe thunderstorms were strongly possible as a result of an encroaching cold front and hot and muggy conditions festering over southeast Ohio. While most of the severe storms occurred east of the Ohio River, there was one storm that produced an EF1 tornado in Athens County during the peak of the afternoon. An NWS Storm Survey team assessed the damage and determined that the tornado tracked just over two miles through the county before lifting back into the mesocyclone. Noted damage included snapped and uprooted trees and power poles along the path.
episodes.184426: A complex of thunderstorms dropped southeast through southern middle Tennessee into northeast Alabama during the midday through mid afternoon hours. A few trees were knocked down as a result of the storms in Moore and Franklin Counties.
episodes.184429: Scattered high-based convection moved from the eastern Texas Panhandle into portions of western and central Oklahoma on the evening of the 11th. Amidst significant downdraft potential energy, scattered damaging wind events (some significant) were noted across the previously mentioned areas.
episodes.184430: Scattered thunderstorms developed in the vicinity of a remnant outflow boundary across portions of southwest Oklahoma during the afternoon/evening of the 12th. Sufficient instability and modest wind shear promoted damaging wind and a few large hail reports across southwest Oklahoma.
episodes.184525: A line of severe storms moved through southeast Minnesota during the evening of August 11th and produced winds in excess of 60 mph as well as quarter sized hail near Rochester (Olmsted County). Broadcast media reported power outages in the City of Winona (Winona County) and Claremont (Dodge County) from fallen trees on power lines.
episodes.184526: A line of severe storms moved through western and central Wisconsin during evening of August 11th, resulting in coinciding corridors of severe reports. In western Wisconsin, volunteer observers reported toppled trees and power lines from severe wind gusts from Buffalo to Richland County. Highest wind gusts included an estimated 80 mph from a NWS storm survey of extensive damage in Westby (Vernon County) and a measured gust of 68 mph in the city of La Crosse (La Crosse County) by an automated weather observation station. In central Wisconsin, volunteer observers reported 60 mph wind gusts and quarter inch hail near Loyal (Clark County).
episodes.184528: Numerous showers and thunderstorms filtered in across portions of Southeast Michigan through the evening of August 11, 2023. The strongest storms were found within the vicinity of or along a warm front, which produced sporadic reports of hail up to an inch and some isolated damaging wind gusts. Prolonged heavy rainfall also led to flooding within Flint which led to multiple road closures. The most significant damage came from a supercell over Perry, MI, which resulted in the production of an EF-1 tornado with maximum wind gusts up to 95 mph. This tornado was on the ground for 12 minutes and started just west of Perry, before moving into the city. Uprooted and sheared trees, damage to outbuildings, and some siding/shingle damage to residential builds were observed. Downed trees also landed on some residential houses and vehicles, resulting in further damage.
episodes.184582: The combined Oklahoma and Texas Panhandles saw quite a bit of moisture return to the area going into the 12th. On both the 12th and the 13th, the combined Panhandles saw widespread rain and thunderstorms across the area. On the 12th some of the storms produced hail up to the size of nickels. Strong winds upwards of 73 mph were measured and several reports of wind damage were made. On the 13th the second round of storms produced hail up to 1.5 in diameter and gusts measured up to 75 mph. Some flooding also occurred on the 13th in Wheeler County.
episodes.184583: The combined Oklahoma and Texas Panhandles saw quite a bit of moisture return to the area going into the 12th. Strong winds upwards of 73 mph were measured and several reports of wind damage were made. On the 13th the second round of storms produced hail up to 1.5 in diameter and gusts measured up to 75 mph. episodes.184626: A typical summer pattern persisted with scattered thunderstorms across the area with a few reports of severe weather.
episodes.184628: A typical summer pattern persisted with scattered thunderstorms across the area with a few reports of severe weather.
episodes.184644: An isolated severe storm developed along an outflow boundary north out of Oklahoma during the late night hours of August 11th over portions of Cowley County. The storm briefly produced quarter to ping ping ball sized hail in Arkansas City along with producing wind damage in Leon before moving eastward and weakening across the Flint Hills.
episodes.184646: A severe thunderstorm developed over Harper County with a swath of elevated showers and storms during the afternoon hours of August 12th. The storm knocked down powerlines in Anthony as wind gusts up to 70 mph impacted the town.
episodes.184676: An overnight line of thunderstorms, from Missouri and Illinois, persisted until reaching Jefferson County. Gusty winds from the line caused isolated tree and property damage in Louisville.
episodes.184693: A typical summer pattern prevailed with scattered thunderstorms producing occasional gusty winds across the coastal waters.
episodes.184736: An upper disturbance moving across a somewhat unstable and highly-sheared environment generated a severe thunderstorm on the evening of the 11th which dropped large hail a few miles northwest of the city of Menominee.
episodes.184753: A warm front translated northward from near the Red River during the day of the 11th. The front extended from north central Oklahoma through southwestern Arkansas by the early evening. Strong to severe thunderstorms developed to the north of this boundary during the evening hours, affecting portions of northwestern Arkansas. The strongest thunderstorms produced damaging wind gusts.
episodes.184867: A mid-level shortwave trough moved across the northern Great Lakes with a belt of stronger flow moving through the southern Great Lakes.  Scattered thunderstorms|developed through midday into the afternoon.  Forecast soundings showed some low-level hodograph curvature. Supercells evolved ahead of the cold front and create a large hail and tornado threat.

Scattered thunderstorms|developed through midday into the afternoon.  Forecast soundings showed some low-level hodograph curvature. episodes.184914: A few showers and thunderstorms developed within the warm sector of a low pressure system across eastern New York during the afternoon and evening hours on August 12, 2023. Most of the activity was located across the mid-Hudson Valley (Ulster and Dutchess counties) where thunderstorms produced several instances of wind damage and some large hail. Localized flash flooding also occurred with these storms. A few other thunderstorms produced some localized wind damage closer to the proximity of a warm front across Herkimer and Warren counties.
episodes.184963: A weakening linear mesoscale convective system moved into southeastern Kansas and was able to produce a damaging wind gust before weakening as it moved east into southern Missouri.
episodes.184968: A weakening linear mesoscale convective system moved into southwestern Missouri and was able to produce a few damaging wind gusts before weakening as it moved east across southern Missouri.
episodes.185031: A strengthening ridge over east Texas and Louisiana kept conditions mostly hot and dry across the Lower Mississippi Valley.  Weak upper-level disturbances in the northwest flow on the periphery of this ridge resulted in numerous showers and thunderstorms across northern sections of the Mid-South during the morning hours of August 12, 2023.  There was enough wind shear aloft and instability to produce an isolated severe storm in northwest Tennessee.
episodes.185043: A cluster of thunderstorms ongoing across parts of central Georgia was forced eastward by a shortwave across the local area, encountering moderate levels of surface-based CAPE, strong low-level lapse rates, high levels of downdraft CAPE and moderate levels of 0-6 km bulk shear. As a result, a few thunderstorms became strong to severe with damaging winds, eventually shifting offshore and tracking across coastal waters.
episodes.185052: Strong storms moved across the marine area and produced high winds.
episodes.185124: A continued pattern of westerly or northwesterly upper level flow produced several consecutive days of severe weather across northeastern and southeastern portions of Central Alabama.
episodes.185127: On August 11, 2023 an unstable air mass with ample deep layer shear supported numerous supercell thunderstorms during the afternoon and evening. These storms produced widespread large hail, along with some damaging wind. A few reports were for greater than 2 inch hail. This event was categorized as a billion dollar disaster in Minnesota by the National Centers for Environmental Information (NCEI).
episodes.185132: Some rogue severe criteria winds developed over the eastern plains.
episodes.185155: Severe storms were not really expected on August the 12th in eastern Kentucky - however locations to our northeast and south/southeast were in more of the risk zone for stronger convection. A MCS developed ahead of a cold front west of the state, and moved fairly quickly eastward into Kentucky. The expectation was that it would weaken as it moved into eastern Kentucky without the availability of  better instability and lift that was located outside of our CWA. However, storms persisted, especially across the southern half of the state. As they made their way into southeast Kentucky, one storm was strong enough to prompt a severe thunderstorm warning for Laurel County. This was the only severe thunderstorm warning of the day, outside of several special weather statements. The warning was warranted, however, as we did end up with a tree down in the community of Barcreek. However, the majority of the reports remained in the higher risk areas, across Central and Eastern Tennessee and points southward, as well as the northeast Ohio Valley into New England.
episodes.185231: A few showers and thunderstorms moved through New Jersey on the afternoon of August 12th. These storms produced damaging wind gusts.
episodes.185232: Two strong systems moved through during the afternoon and evening on August 12th, with strong to severe thunderstorms producing damaging wind gusts and large hail.
episodes.185276: With a lingering upper-level trough across the area, a weak surface convergence axis and diurnal destabilization produced a few late afternoon thunderstorms across southwest Minnesota and into northwest Iowa in the evening. Stronger cells produced marginally large hail, and some damaging wind gusts with a strong sub-cloud dry layer.
episodes.185285: On the evening hours of August 11th into early morning August 12th, storms brought hail, damaging winds, flash flooding, and even a brief tornado to northern Missouri.
episodes.185291: An upper level shortwave traveling across the region, paired with modest MUCAPE and moisture above the midlevels allowed for sub-severe to severe hail across portions of Northern Iowa through the late evening. Large hail of 2-3 inches occurred in Humboldt and Hancock counties with these storms.
episodes.185374: A couple of broken lines of thunderstorms moved across western North Carolina during the afternoon and early evening. A few of the storms produced brief severe weather, mainly in the form of damaging wind gusts.
episodes.185375: A couple of broken lines of thunderstorms moved across upstate South Carolina during the late afternoon and early evening. A few of the storms produced swaths of strong-to-damaging wind gusts.
episodes.185376: A couple of broken lines of thunderstorms moved across northeast Georgia during the late afternoon and early evening. A few of the storms produced briefing damaging wind gusts.
episodes.186604: An occluded surface low meandered near the eastern shore of Lake Superior during the late morning through early evening of the 12th. Simultaneously, the trailing cold front swept southeastward from southeastern Lower MI and northern IN to central Lake Erie and north-central/west-central portions of OH. Multiple multicell and supercell thunderstorms occurred along and ahead of the cold front in northern OH. These storms produced severe hail, damaging convective gusts, and two tornadoes in a warm sector comprised of moderate to strong MUCAPE and effective bulk shear, respectively, mixed-layer lifting condensation levels near 750 to 1500 meters AGL, and strong surface-based effective storm-relative helicity near 150 meters squared per second squared.
episodes.186605: An occluded surface low meandered near the eastern shore of Lake Superior during the late morning through early evening of the 12th. Simultaneously, the trailing cold front swept southeastward from southeastern Lower MI and northern IN to central Lake Erie and north-central/west-central portions of OH. Multiple multicell thunderstorms occurred over Lake Erie, along and ahead of the cold front. These storms produced gale-force peak convective wind gusts along the OH shore as the storms encountered moderate to strong MUCAPE and effective bulk shear, respectively.
episodes.186613: Overnight August 11th into August 12th, discrete supercells congealed into a convective complex. This system produced widespread wind damage from northeast Missouri and west central Illinois as far south as the St. Louis Metropolitan Area.
episodes.186614: Overnight August 11th into August 12th, discrete supercells congealed into a convective complex. This system produced widespread wind damage from northeast Missouri and west central Illinois as far south as the St. Louis Metropolitan Area.
episodes.186796: An occluded surface low meandered near the eastern shore of Lake Superior during the late morning through early evening of the 12th. Simultaneously, the trailing cold front swept southeastward from southeastern Lower MI and northern IN to central Lake Erie and north-central/west-central portions of OH. Multiple multicell thunderstorms and a supercell thunderstorm occurred ahead of the cold front in northwest PA. These storms produced small hail, damaging convective gusts, and a tornado in a warm sector comprised of moderate to strong MUCAPE and effective bulk shear, respectively, mixed-layer lifting condensation levels near 750 to 1500 meters AGL, and strong surface-based effective storm-relative helicity near 150 meters squared per second squared.

The leading edge of the storm impacted Rensselaer and Palmyra at nearly the same time, causing widespread damage to a farm and destroying a garage in Rensselaer. Several trees were downed there as well, and a 10 inch diameter tree fell in Palmyra.

An isolated thunderstorm produced extensive wind damage in rural northeastern Childress County near the intersection of US Highway 62 and Farm to Market Road 1642. Several power poles were snapped and a center pivot irrigation system was overturned.

A trained spotter submitted photos of a large 8-10 inch tree limb down at their residence. The spotter noted a large evergreen was down near the Dollar General and multiple smaller limbs less than 4 inches in diameter were down throughout town. This occurred as the leading edge of the line of storms surged as it passed over town.
There were numerous reports of fallen trees and one report of downed power lines between Atlas/Summer Hill and Pleasant Hill as the leading edge of the line of storms passed over Pike County.

Numerous large maple trees sustained damage with one tree blown over and another split in half. This occurred as a bowing segment largely independent of the primary line of storms passed over the location.

The tornado touched down 5 miles southwest of Middletown, on the west side of Swope School Road, just north of intersection with Highway A. In this location, several trees and tree branches were blown down. The tornado moved to the southeast, crossing Highway A and then as it crossed Trinity Church Road, several large tree limbs were snapped off and blocked the road. The tornado continued to the southeast for almost two more miles with additional minor tree damage before lifting and dissipating near the intersection of Nagel Road and Poppy Road, about 4 miles south southwest of Middletown. Overall the tornado was rated EF0 with a path length of 2.54 miles and a max path width of 40 yards. No deaths or injuries were reported.

There was widespread tree damage across St. Charles County. The damage was reported in Flint Hill, Wentzville, O'Fallon, St. Peters, St. Charles, Weldon Springs and Cottleville. Also, in Flint Hill there was minor shingle damage to a few homes. In O'Fallon, a large branch snapped off and damaged a vinyl fence. This EF-1 tornado began near the center of Hickman, in the Terrace Drive and Sunset Street area. Damage to trees and power lines occurred in this neighborhood. This tornado tracked to the east-southeast, with more tree damage on Bayou Street and Johnson Lane. A large tree fell onto a home on Myron Cory Drive. The tornado crossed Kentucky 125 and proceeded to 7th Street, where the most significant cluster of damage occurred with several trees uprooted, portions of a few trees snapped, and power line damage. One of the trees fell onto a car. The storm was at its peak width around Kentucky 125 and 7th Street. Additional damage to trees occurred on Nelson Street and Harrison Street. The damage path ended at this point, with the tornado lifting after moving into open areas east of Nelson Street. Peak winds were estimated near 105 mph.

Trees were blocking sections of Highway 125 near and southeast of Hickman. Several trees were down southwest of Cayce. There was minor structural damage in this part of Fulton County, mostly roofs off outbuildings.

This EF-1 tornado began with a cluster of damage along Kentucky 307 just south of Johnson Rd, including on Bizzle Road and Laine Road. Around two dozen trees were blown down, and a grain bin was destroyed on Laine Road. This was the strongest and widest portion of the tornado track. The tornado proceeded northeastward, with damage to a portion of a tree line south of Johnson Road. Large branches and smaller limbs were found on Rushton Road and Kentucky 1529. A tree fell on a house along Highway 1529. A large section of a tree fell onto a home on Wilson Road. The tornado appeared to have lifted shortly after crossing Wilson Road. Peak winds were estimated near 105 mph.

The tornado first touched down in the vicinity of west Espy Street and Robinson Avenue. Some minor tree limb damage was noted, with some sheet metal damage to buildings in this area, including roof damage to one structure between west Espy Street and U.S. Route 68. Damage was more significant and concentrated in a neighborhood near Detroit Street and Main Street, especially between Railroad Street and Letson Street. Numerous trees and large limbs were downed and numerous homes and garages had at least some minor roof or fascia damage. The winds were likely the strongest just north of Letson Street, where one garage was flattened and another outbuilding had its roof and second floor removed. Debris from these structures could be found at least a quarter mile downstream. Winds at this location were estimated to be about 90 mph. Additional tree damage and minor structural damage was noted on the east side of Main Street, extending from near the Hardin County Sheriff's Office through Brumm Street.||Additional tree damage was observed on the north side of the Scioto River, near and south of Lick Street. This includes one grove of trees south of the end of Stevens Street, with several tree tops snapped off. The tornado then traversed an uninhabited area but minor tree damage was noted near the intersection of Bales Road and County Road 175. In addition, small pieces of insulation were found near this intersection and in the field to the east. This is where the tornado ended.

A tornado touched down just north of Interstate 80 along Nescopeck|Creek. A narrow alley of numerous downed or snapped trees occurred,|roughly following Overlook Road and then West Hollow Road, where|a convergent and at times oppositional tree pattern was observed. |The tornado departed West Hollow Road only to reemerge crossing |Route 93, where a few hundred small apple trees were pushed over in|an orchard, and a front porch roof was lifted up and over a house, |while peeling back a portion of the primary roof of the residence. |A large tree top was also lofted, and thrown to Zenith Road, to the |left of the tornado path. The tornado intensified while moving along |Hobbie Road, with numerous large trunk snaps, including several trees |damaging a residence with a destroyed shed. The yard had several |missiles in the form of small branches impaling into the ground. |The tornado finally lifted shortly after, before reaching the |intersection of Hobbie Road and Wapwallopen Road.

A tornado briefly touched down along the south shore of the East Branch Delaware River near Fishs Eddy causing damage to trees. An eyewitness reported seeing his 75-100 foot hemlock tree twist and snap off about halfway up the trunk. Another eyewitness captured video of a rotating wall cloud in the general vicinity of this |area of damage. The tornado crossed O&W Road, proceeding uphill causing further damage to some trees in the forest and powerlines along Hubbell Hill Road. Due to extremely steep terrain, the evidence of further tornado damage was unobtainable through these wooded areas. Additional tree damage was observed at the intersection of O&W Road and Halls Island Road to the southeast of East Branch. The tornado is believed to have skipped through the mountainous area before lifting over the Beaver Kill. No further damage was noted or reported across the river toward Baxter Mountain.

An EF1 tornado with maximum winds up to 100 mph touched down near Angel Ridge Road in Athens County. The tornado tracked east-northeast crossing Gura Road, Long Run Road, and North Coolville Ridge Road before lifting just past Kincade Road. Damage was limited to snapped and uprooted trees and some snapped power poles along the path, with the worst damage occurring in a 300 yard wide swath along Long Run Road. This is the seventh documented tornado in Athens County and the first since 2018.
